content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "Display (5) is ill-formed: its O(n+m) term absorbs the very linear term 4c(c-e)n it isolates, and the correct coefficients used in each case are asserted, not computed.", "errors": [{"description": "In (5) the highlighted linear term 4c(c-e)n is not the actual coefficient of n in the expanded expression (that is 2c^2-4ce+2c(x_0-y_0)); the value 4c(c-e) only emerges after using the near-diagonal relation em \u2248 cn. Moreover the stated O(n+m) remainder subsumes all linear terms, making (5) vacuous as written. The correct per-case coefficients (4cq(c-e)k, 4c(c-e)n_k+O(1)) are asserted without derivation, though both are in fact correct.", "quote": "(c n - e m)^2 \\;+\\; \\underbrace{4c(c-e)n}_{\\text{linear in }n} \\;+\\; O(n+m) \\;\\ge\\; 0 \\qquad (5)"}, {"description": "The 'swap the roles of c and e by symmetry' step is justified only by a vague parenthetical; inequality (4) is not symmetric in x,y, and one must instead re-apply (4) with x taken from the e-orbit and y from the c-orbit. The relabelling does work, but is not spelled out.", "quote": "we can swap the roles of $c$ and $e$ by symmetry (the inequality is symmetric in $x,y$ up to the roles of $c,e$ and the sign of the linear term)"}, {"description": "The limit discussion in Step 4 is muddled (an irrelevant parenthetical about b_n \u2192 0 and a wrong 'right side tends to c^2 + 4c lim b_n'), although the conclusion that the RHS of (7) is \u2265 c^2 > 0 while the LHS \u2192 0 is trivially correct.", "quote": "while the right side tends to $c^2 + 4c \\lim b_n$ (or $c^2 + 2c \\cdot 0$ if a subsequence of $b_n$ tends to $0$, which is impossible because then $a_n \\to 0$ as well and the right side $\\to c^2 > 0$)"}], "notes": "Correct answer f(x)=x+c, c\u22650. Key steps (x=f(y) forcing equality, d(f(x))=d(x), orbit positivity, two-orbit Dirichlet argument, connectedness argument, verification) are all sound; only computational presentation is sloppy."}
